title: [Practice Tests Plus] - The creation of lasting memories

parts.title: practice test plus 3 test 1 sec 3
parts.passageHtml:
{[Many studies of the brain processes underlying the creation of memory consolidation (lasting memories) have involved giving various human and animal subjects treatment, while training them to perform a task.][236447]} {[These have contributed greatly to our understanding.][236477]}

{[In pioneering studies using goldfish, Bernard Agranoff found that protein synthesis inhibitors injected after training caused the goldfish to forget what they had learned.][236486]} {[In other experiments, he administered protein synthesis inhibitors immediately before the fish were trained.][236511]} {[The remarkable finding was that the fish learned the task completely normally, but forgot it within a few hours - that is, the protein synthesis inhibitors blocked memory consolidation, but did not influence short-term memory.][236526]}

{[There is now extensive evidence that short-term memory is spared by many kinds of treatments, including electro-convulsive therapy (ECT), that block memory consolidation.][236562]} {[On the other hand, and equally importantly, neuroscientist Ivan Izquierdo found that many drug treatments can block short-term memory without blocking memory consolidation.][236588]} {[Contrary to the hypothesis put forward by Canadian psychologist Donald Hebb, in 1949, long-term memory does not require short-term memory, and vice versa.][236612]}

{[Such findings suggest that our experiences create parallel, and possibly independent stages of memory, each with a different life span.][236637]} {[All of this evidence from clinical and experimental studies strongly indicates that the brain handles recent and remote memory in different ways; but why does it do that?][236657]}

{[We obviously need to have memory that is created rapidly: reacting to an ever and rapidly changing environment requires that.][236689]} {[For example, most current building codes require that the heights of all steps in a staircase be equal.][236700]} {[After taking a couple of steps, up or down, we implicitly remember the heights of the steps and assume that the others will be the same.][236718]} {[If they are not the same, we are very likely to trip and fall.][236743]} {[Lack of this kind of rapidly created implicit memory would be bad for us and for insurance companies, but perhaps good for lawyers.][236758]} {[It would be of little value to us if we remembered the heights of the steps only after a delay of many hours, when the memory becomes consolidated.][236781]}

{[The hypothesis that lasting memory consolidates slowly over time is supported primarily by clinical and experimental evidence that the formation of long-term memory is influenced by treatments and disorders affecting brain functioning.][236810]} {[There are also other kinds of evidence indicating more directly that the memories consolidate over time after learning.][236843]} {[Avi Kami and Dov Sagi reported that the performance of human subjects trained in a visual skill did not improve until eight hours after the training was completed, and that improvement was even greater the following day.][236862]} {[Furthermore, the skill was retained for several years.][236899]}

{[Studies using human brain imaging to study changes in neural activity induced by learning have also reported that the changes continue to develop for hours after learning.][236909]} {[In an innovative study using functional imaging of the brain, Reza Shadmehr and Henry Holcomb examined brain activity in several brain regions shortly after human subjects were trained in a motor learning task requiring arm and hand movements.][236937]} {[They found that while the performance of the subjects remained stable for several hours after completion of the training, their brain activity did not; different regions of the brain were predominantly active at different times over a period of several hours after the training.][236974]} {[The activity shifted from the prefrontal cortex to two areas known to be involved in controlling movements, the motor cortex and cerebellar cortex.][237018]} {[Consolidation of the motor skill appeared to involve activation of different neural systems that increased the stability of the brain processes underlying the skill.][237042]}

{[There is also evidence that learning-induced changes in the activity of neurons in the cerebral cortex continue to increase for many days after the training.][237068]} {[In an extensive series of studies using rats with electrodes implanted in the auditory cortex, Norman Weinberger reported that, after a tone of specific frequency was paired a few times with footshock, neurons in the rats’ auditory cortex responded more to that specific tone and less to other tones of other frequencies.][237095]} {[Even more interestingly, the selectivity of the neurons’ response to the specific tone used in training continued to increase for several days after the training was terminated.][237145]}

{[It is not intuitively obvious why our lasting memories consolidate slowly.][237174]} {[Certainly, one can wonder why we have a form of memory that we have to rely on for many hours, days or a lifetime, that is so susceptible to disruption shortly after it is initiated.][237186]} {[Perhaps the brain system that consolidates long-term memory over time was a late development in vertebrate evolution.][237219]} {[Moreover, maybe we consolidate memories slowly because our mammalian brains are large and enormously complex.][237236]} {[We can readily reject these ideas.][237252]} {[All species of animals studied to date have both short and long-term memory; and all are susceptible to retrograde amnesia.][237259]} {[Like humans, birds, bees, and molluscs, as well as fish and rats, make long-term memory slowly.][237280]} {[Consolidation of memory clearly emerged early in evolution, and was conserved.][237296]}

{[Although there seems to be no compelling reason to conclude that a biological system such as a brain could not quickly make a lasting memory, the fact is that animal brains do not.][237309]} {[Thus, memory consolidation must serve some very important adaptive function or functions.][237340]} {[There is considerable evidence suggesting that the slow consolidation is adaptive because it enables neurobiological processes occurring shortly after learning to influence the strength of memory for experiences.][237351]} {[The extensive evidence that memory can be enhanced, as well as impaired, by treatments administered shortly after training, provides intriguing support for this hypothesis.][237380]}

questions.explanationHtml:
1 
A
Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight, ý nói: protein synthesis inhibitors được tiêm vào sau khi luyện tập (protein synthesis inhibitors injected after training)
protein synthesis inhibitors được tiêm vào ngay trước khi luyện tập (he administered protein synthesis inhibitors immediately before the fish were trained)
=> chọn A/ Việc tiêm cho goldfish ở những thời điểm khác nhau (at different stages).

options.text: drug treatments do not normally affect short-term memories.
long-term memories build upon short-term memories.
short and long-term memories are formed by separate processes.
CT treatment affects both short- and long-term memories.

questions.explanationHtml:
2 
C
Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight, ý nói: những nghiên cứu này cho thấy những trải nghiệm của chúng ta (Such findings suggest that our experiences), tạo ra những giai đoạn song song và độc lập trong trí nhớ, (create parallel, and possibly independent stages of memory,) và mỗi giai đoạn lại có một vòng đời khác nhau (each with a different life span).
=> chọn C/ trí nhớ ngắn và dài của chúng ta được tạo nên bởi những quá trình khác nhau => không liên quan (short and long-term memories are formed by separate processes)

options.text: Prompt memory formation underlies the performance of everyday tasks.
Routine tasks can be carried out unconsciously.
Physical accidents can impair the function of memory.
Complex information such as regulations cannot be retained by the memory.

questions.explanationHtml:
3 
A
Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight, ý nói: sau khi bước vài bước lên xuống,(after taking a couple of steps, up or down,) chúng ta có khả năng tự nhớ chiều cao của các bậc thang ( we implicitly remember the heights of the steps) và mặc định là các bậc khác cũng giống vậy ( and assume that the others will be the same).
=> chọn câu A/ sự hình thành những trí nhớ tức thời (prompt memory formation) nhấn mạnh việc thực hiện các hành động hàng ngày (underlies the performance of everyday tasks.)
*Việc bước cầu thang là việc hàng ngày và bước vài bước sẽ nhớ chiều cao bậc thang.

options.text: cast doubt on existing hypotheses.
related only to short-term memory.
were based on tasks involving hearing.
confirmed other experimental findings.

questions.explanationHtml:
4 
D
Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight, ý nói: trong thí nghiệm của Kami and Sagi, sự thể hiện (performance) của những người được luyên về "visual skill" không tăng liền mà sau 8 tiếng mới tắng. => điều này đúng với nhận định ở câu đầu đoạn "lasting memory consolidates slowly over time" => Chọn D

options.text: Different areas of the brain were activated by different tasks.
Activity in the brain gradually moved from one area to other areas.
Subjects continued to get better at a task after training had finished.
Treatment given to subjects improved their performance on a task.

Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight, ý nói: các hoạt của não di chuyển từ "prefrontal cortex" đến "motor cortex" và "cerebellar cortex" => chọn câu B/ hoạt động của não được chuyển từ 1 vùng đến các vùng khác.

Questions 6 - 10:

Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage?

YES                if the statement agrees with the views of the writer

NO                 if the statement contradicts the views of the writer

options.text: YES
NO
NOT GIVEN

questions.text: The training which Kami and Sagi’s subjects were given was repeated over several days.
questions.explanationHtml:
6 
Not given
Ý này không được nhắc đến trong bài.
Bài đọc chỉ nhắc đến ý bên dưới.
Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight, ý nói: sự thể hiện của những người tham gia thí nghiệm về khả năng hình ảnh (the performance of human subjects trained in a visual skill), chỉ được tăng lên 8 giờ sau khi thí nghiệm kết thúc (did not improve until eight hours after the training was completed) và tăng mạnh hơn vào ngày hôm sau (, and that improvement was even greater the following day.)

questions.text: The rats in Weinberger’s studies learned to associate a certain sound with a specific experience.
questions.explanationHtml:
7 
Yes
Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight, ý nói: sau khi 1 âm thanh tại 1 tầng số nhất định (after a tone of specific frequency) được nối với trải nghiệm "footshock" ( was paired a few times with footshock) thì các "neurons" ở não của các bạn chuột (neurons in the rats’ auditory cortex) đáp ứng với âm thanh đó nhiều hơn là đáp ứng với các âm thanh ở tầng số khác (responded more to that specific tone and less to other tones of other frequencies.)
Câu 7/ Các bạn chuột trong thí nghiệm của Weinberger học cách liên hệ 1 âm thanh và 1 trải nghiệm.=>đúng với ý trong bài => Yes

questions.text: The results of Weinberger’s studies indicated that the strength of the rats’ learned associations increases with time.
questions.explanationHtml:
8 
Yes
Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight, ý nói: số lượng neuron mà "phản ứng" với 1 cái "tone" được sử dụng trong "training" vẫn còn tăng lên sau nhiều ngày, sau khi thí nghiệm kết thúc.
Trong câu hỏi: nói là sức mạnh của việc kết nối (associations) tăng theo thời gian. => đúng với ý trong bài => Yes

questions.text: It is easy to see the evolutionary advantage of the way lasting memories in humans are created.
questions.explanationHtml:
9 
No
Trong bài đọc, phần được highlight, ý nói: việc hiểu lý do tại sao những trí nhớ dài hạn "lasting memories" được phát triển chậm rãi (consolidate slowly) là rất khó khăn (It is not intuitively obvious)
=> Tuy nhiên trong câu 9/ lại nói là rất dễ hiểu được sự phát triển của "lasting memories" => No

questions.text: Long-term memories in humans are more stable than in many other species.
questions.explanationHtml:
10 
Not Given
Trong bài đọc nhận định là những loài động vật khác nhau được nghiên cứu đều có trí nhớ tạm thời và trí nhớ dài hạn. 
 
Tuy nhiên, bài đọc không nêu ra là trí nhớ dài hạn của con người (long-term memories in humans) thì ổn định hơn các loài động vật khác.(Đây là ý của câu 10) => Not Given

E lengthy
F new
G recently
H small
I quick
  

Long-term memory

Various researchers have examined the way lasting memories are formed. Laboratory experiments usually involve teaching subjects to do something 11 and treating them with mild electric shocks or drugs. Other studies monitor behaviour after a learning experience, or use sophisticated equipment to observe brain activity.

The results are generally consistent: they show that lasting memories are the result of a 12 and complex biological process.

The fact that humans share this trait with other species, including animals with 13 brains, suggests that it developed 14 in our evolutionary history.
